title: Śrī Rāmcaritmānas (Tulsīdās)
author: tulsidas
attributionNote: Śrī Rāmcaritmānas (Tulsīdās), attributed to Goswāmī Tulsīdās, as Heritage IITKanpur's Scripture Server catalogues it (RCM), on its own shelf.
description: The Rāmcaritmānas, "the lake of the deeds of Rāma", is Gosvāmī Tulsīdās's retelling of the Rāma story, composed in Awadhi in the sixteenth century in seven kāṇḍas of caupāī and dohā verses meant to be sung. Its subject is Rāma's life and character; its purpose is devotion (bhakti) to Rāma and, through it, a guide to living. It draws on the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa but tells the story as an act of love and surrender, moving constantly between narrative and prayer, and belongs to the bhakti poetry of North India that set devotion in the people's own language. It asks of its reader faith and love more than learning, and is recited in homes and in great public recitations. The summary above is the one Heritage IITKanpur's Scripture Server publishes for the text, and the server's own metadata records it as AI-assisted (claude-opus-5-5); an editor's note for the work itself is still to be written.
historicalContext: Read in the Heritage Scripture Server corpus, which continues the Gita Supersite built at IIT Kanpur: the text, its classical commentaries and the translations the server may serve are held together there.
availabilityNote: The outline is held: 7 chapter(s) and 1074 verse address(es), read from the server's own catalogue. The verses are not stored — the licence forbids bulk harvesting and database reconstruction — and are streamed from the API one verse at a time as the work is read, with the attribution HCAL-1.1 requires and the server's own quota and licence notice.
